units.title: Matrices and Determinants
topics: Eight uses of matrices in computing

sections.title: Eight uses of matrices in computing

summary: Matrix multiplication combines rows with columns, is associative but not commutative.
The determinant measures scaling and invertibility; row operations compute it efficiently.
A matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is non-zero; inverses come from the adjoint or Gauss–Jordan.

units.title: Systems of Linear Equations
topics: Three pictures of a linear system

sections.title: Three pictures of a linear system

summary: Elimination reduces any system to echelon form and then solves by back-substitution.
Rank decides the number of solutions; free variables parametrise infinite families.
Cramer's rule and inverses give formulas but elimination is the practical method.
Applications range from curve fitting to chemistry, circuits and regression.

units.title: Vector Spaces and Linear Transformations
topics: The four subspaces in one picture
Eight uses of vector spaces and linear maps

sections.title: The four subspaces in one picture
Eight uses of vector spaces and linear maps

summary: Vector spaces abstract the idea of vector; subspaces, span, independence, basis and dimension organise them.
Rank–nullity ties the solutions of A X = 0 to the rank of A.
Linear maps are matrices; their kernel and image measure what is lost and what is reached.
Orthogonal bases and projections give coordinates, Gram–Schmidt and least squares.

units.title: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors and Diagonalisation
summary: Eigenvectors are the directions a matrix only stretches; eigenvalues are the stretch factors.
The characteristic polynomial finds them; trace and determinant give quick checks.
Diagonalisation turns matrix powers into powers of numbers; symmetric matrices diagonalise orthogonally.
Markov chains, PageRank, PCA, stability and vibration analysis are all eigenvalue problems.

units.title: Vectors in Space, Lines and Planes
topics: A plane, its normal and the distance to a point
Eight uses of vectors in space

sections.title: A plane, its normal and the distance to a point
Eight uses of vectors in space

summary: The dot product measures alignment and angles; the cross product measures area and gives normals.
The triple product measures volume and tests coplanarity.
Lines and planes have vector, parametric and Cartesian forms, with simple distance and angle formulas.
The same operations drive lighting, culling and reflection in graphics, and torque and work in physics.
